title: Real sign-in: device login for the CLI (the local reading)
summary: Better Auth 1.7.15's deviceAuthorization is in the server's auth (client acme-cli only, table auth_device_code, a 5 second polling interval), and the generated server mounts Better Auth's routes at /api/auth. The generated CLI's session sign-in --env <env> runs the device flow: it prints the code and where to approve it, polls with an Effect Schedule that backs off on slow_down, keeps the session in the config folder (ACME_CONFIG_DIR) and prints signed in. session show --env <env> uses the kept session and prints the person. The real staging sign-in is the cloud pass.
proves: On a real local world, the generated CLI signs in by device code; ada claims and approves the code with her own session and no browser, and session show prints her. Bob approving ada's claimed code is a 403, another client id is refused, a poll before the interval is slow_down, a code is single-use, and no token or password is printed.

captions.01-fails-first: The check before the build: the generated server has no /api/auth, so it fails.
captions.02-device-sign-in: The check after: two tests on a real local world and the generated CLI.
